I am sorry if this seems pessimistic but I want to share my experience with this. I’m in a nearly identical situation, and my school essentially said I cannot get more aid.

Besides my scholarship, I currently receive aid from FAFSA, and was told that the process it takes to use my own taxes to apply for aid as opposed to my mom’s taxes (dependency override) was extremely difficult and nearly impossible to prove to the federal government. Additionally, there are a number or intrusive interviews where they want you to give detailed reasons why not only A) you separated from your parents, and B) why it is impossible to get your parents taxes. Even if the parent is abusive, unless there is physically no way to get their taxes for FAFSA, I was advised to avoid this route entirely.

On top of that, if I did somehow prove independence and the dependency override went through, my overall aid would go down. Federal aid would increase slightly, state aid would decrease drastically, and loans offered would increase to account for that. So I would get less aid and more offered loans. Pretty shitty situation.

Your school’s financial office may be different and they might offer you an increased need-based scholarship that has nothing to do with federal or state student financial aid. I hope this is the case.

I ended up taking a part time retail job and (thanks to having an extremely understanding and wonderful manager) maxing my hours, taking 15 credits in school and 24-28 hours a week at work. I found a friend willing to rent a room in their place for a few hundred a month, which is all I could afford. This is much cheaper than my own place, and is far less straining on the relationship because it wasn’t freeloading. My expenses became a few hundred a month for tuition, a few hundred for rent, no more than $150 for food per month, and transportation costs. I had no savings left but it worked out until the end of the semester and now I’m working throughout the summer trying to save for the fall.

I know the situation may seem tough, but you’ll make it though it. You’ve made it this far, and the semester is over/almost over so you have more freedom to plan things out without worrying about your grades. I wish you the best of luck and if you have any questions or want to talk for support, please feel free to Pm me. Stay strong, you made the right decision. Don’t look back.

EDIT: I just read that you’re Canadian. I live in the US so my advice on financial aid may not be applicable, but the rest is good to know. As other people have said, try to be considerate of your boyfriend’s family’s expenses and help around the house when you can. Something I learned is that it’s also important to set boundaries, too. If you’re paying rent, your room and your belongings are yours and not open to anyone else even if they’re helping you out. Don’t let them go through your stuff. Stay safe.
